requirements.requirement: Firewall service (firewalld) is enabled persistently (survives reboot) on node1
requirements.summary: firewalld was already active/enabled; systemctl is-enabled firewalld=enabled confirmed pre-reboot, and post full-node-restart (boot_id changed 583ddd53...->b519ab7d...) firewalld was again active+enabled with identical zone config, directly demonstrating persistence across a real reboot.

firewall-cmd --list-all (permanent and runtime, pre- and post-reboot) shows 'ssh' service enabled; nft ruleset shows 'tcp dport 22 accept' in filter_IN_public_allow both before and after reboot; sshd remained active/listening and the verification session itself connected over SSH post-reboot.
8080/tcp was added permanently and confirmed in both permanent and runtime firewall-cmd output; nft ruleset shows 'tcp dport 8080 accept' pre- and post-reboot.

The extraneous cockpit service was removed and the nft ruleset dump shows filter_IN_public_allow contains only tcp dport 22, tcp dport 8080, and an IPv6 link-local DHCPv6 exception, with filter_IN_public and filter_INPUT falling through to 'reject with icmpx admin-prohibited' for everything else. This structural rule inspection directly demonstrates the deny-by-default behavior for the external (enp1s0) zone.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — a persistent firewalld configuration on node1 allowing only SSH and TCP 8080 and rejecting other inbound traffic — are directly supported by pre- and post-reboot firewall-cmd and nft ruleset output, and persistence was verified through an actual full-node restart with a confirmed boot-identity change and identical recovered firewall state. The only quality issue is a same-host curl connectivity test that was methodologically flawed (loopback bypasses zone filtering) but was not used as the executor's basis for its final claims, plus minor leftover temp/log files from that test.
limitations: The 'reject unrelated inbound' claim rests on structural nft ruleset inspection rather than an external network probe from outside node1, since no second node was available to test from; this is standard for this environment but is indirect versus an end-to-end external connection test.

The executor's own curl-based dual-port test (ports 8080 and 9091) produced a misleading 200/200 result because both requests traversed the loopback interface, which firewalld exempts from zone filtering; this does not contradict the final configuration but the test itself was not a valid demonstration of blocking behavior.

Minor temp-file residue (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9091.log, /tmp/http9091.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) from the flawed test and reboot scheduling remained on node1 after task completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor started two throwaway python http.server test processes on ports 8080 and 9091 (cmd-97f8faea323e49db, cmd-d29540c696ac4826) to probe firewall behavior; this test was flawed because curl was issued from the same node, so both requests traversed the loopback interface which firewalld's zone rules explicitly exempt ('iifname lo accept'), making the '9091 status=200' result misleading rather than evidence of a bypass — the executor correctly did not rely on this curl output for its final claims, using the nft ruleset dump instead. The test processes were killed in cmd-60884dd4c0524fd6, but their artifact files (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9091.log, /tmp/http9091.pid) and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind, visible as residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is a bounded, low-risk, non-destructive mutation that was mostly but not fully cleaned up.
